query: What kinds of tickets create heavier agent workload?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: The time an agent spends handling/resolving a ticket is a genuine constitutive aspect of workload burden -- the temporal/effort-duration facet of how much work a ticket imposes.

per_column.name: priority_score
per_column.rationale: Priority is an attribute assigned to the ticket that predicts or drives how much attention it gets; it is not itself a part of the agent's workload. It is an external driver, not an aspect of the burden.

per_column.name: updated_after_close
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for post-close updates (constant 0 here) does not constitute an aspect of workload burden; it is a degenerate data-quality/rework indicator that carries no information and does not decompose the concept.

per_column.name: workload_index
per_column.rationale: A composite 'index' is a re-aggregation of the whole concept rather than a distinct non-overlapping part; it restates the burden as a single scalar and overlaps heavily with resolution_hours (its values track that column), violating meronymy.

judge.rationale: Only resolution_hours is a true constitutive facet of workload burden (effort/duration). priority_score is an external predictor/driver, updated_after_close is a degenerate irrelevant flag, and workload_index restates the whole concept as a composite and overlaps with resolution_hours, harming mutual exclusivity. As a facet set it captures essentially one aspect (time/effort) and omits other constitutive facets such as cognitive/complexity load, interaction/communication volume, number of reassignments or touches, and multitasking/concurrency, so exhaustiveness is very low.
